title: Domes wide open
caption: Auxiliary Telescopes and the Magellanic Clouds, Very Large Telescope
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Three telescopes with their domes open work in the foreground of this night scene. They are three of the four movable Auxiliary Telescopes at ESO's Very Large Telescope, each with a mirror 1.8 meters across. In the center of the sky two bright patches mark the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds.
The Magellanic Clouds are neighboring galaxies to our own, and they are visible to the naked eye. Although they look like soft patches of light, each is a separate galaxy made up of its own stars.

The Very Large Telescope is based on Cerro Paranal in the Atacama Desert of northern Chile. The Auxiliary Telescopes are smaller than the main Unit Telescopes, but because they can be moved they can be placed in different positions on the platform. With domes wide open, as they are in the photograph, they are observing the sky above.

understand.summary: A ground-based landscape photograph by M. Claro for ESO, taken in visible light. The colors are those the camera recorded.
understand.eye: The Magellanic Clouds are visible to the naked eye, but a camera exposure makes them look brighter and more detailed than they would to someone on the platform.
